payout_quote: Find federal and state laws and incentives for alternative fuels and vehicles, air quality, fuel efficiency, and other transportation-related topics. Termination: 'This section [30C] shall not apply to any property placed in service after June 30, 2026.'
timing: State and utility EV-charger incentive timing varies by program. The federal 30C credit expired for property placed in service after June 30, 2026 (claims for pre-deadline installs go on the 2026 tax return).
eligibility: Set by each state/utility program (many are utility-customer-only or income-targeted). The expired federal 30C credit was worth 30% up to $1,000 for home chargers and required installation in an eligible low-income-community or non-urban census tract.
catches: The federal EV charger tax credit (30%, up to $1,000) EXPIRED June 30, 2026 — do not promise it for new installations.
What remains are state and utility rebates that vary by location; many areas have nothing.
Every incentive requires buying and installing a charger ($500-$2,000+) first — a discount on spending, not money earned.
AFDC's own disclaimer: verify each incentive is still applicable before acting.
steps: Go to https://afdc.energy.gov/laws and search incentives for your state, filtering for electric-vehicle charging infrastructure.
Open each listed program and confirm it is currently funded and accepting applications — do not rely on the AFDC summary alone.
Also check your electric utility's website for charger rebates not listed federally.
Buy and install a qualifying Level 2 charger per the program's rules (some require pre-approval or a licensed electrician).
Submit the rebate application or claim the tax treatment per the program's instructions; keep all receipts and installation dates.
biggest_catch: The federal EV charger tax credit (30%, up to $1,000) expired June 30, 2026 — what remains are state/utility rebates that vary by location, and all of them require buying and installing a $500-$2,000+ charger first; it is a discount, not income.
notes: CORRECTION vs the route's framing: the $1,000 top end was the federal 30C credit, now expired. State/utility charger rebates are live in many areas via the AFDC database. PRODUCT NOTE: charger incentives reduce purchase cost; they are not earnings.
